solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Poet's wretched dogs covered in do

indicators.note: something covered in a wrapping sits inside it, so one word goes within the other

blocks.note: to do is to act; this word is split open
curs are mongrel dogs

explanation.surface: A poet describes some miserable dogs smeared in muck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'do' looks like a noun for mess or dung, but it is the verb meaning to perform.
explanation.definitionFit: Accurst is an archaic, poetic spelling of accursed, meaning doomed or miserable, hence the 'Poet's' tag.

clue.text: Wild ox half destroyed northern town in Australia

indicators.note: with half of it destroyed only one half of the word survives
the surviving letters are placed inside the abbreviation that follows

blocks.note: AUS is the abbreviation for Australia; it is split open
Rochdale is a town in Greater Manchester, in the north of England

explanation.surface: A rampaging wild ox wrecks half a town in the north of Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'northern town in Australia' reads as one place, but the town is English and Australia is a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: The aurochs was the large wild ox of Europe, the extinct ancestor of domestic cattle.

clue.text: Another suggestion: table leg also needs fixing

indicators.note: a word that needs fixing is broken, so its letters must be put back in a new order

blocks.note: a counter is a table or bench in a shop or kitchen
a leg props something up, so it is a prop or support
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A furniture repair report: the table has a dodgy leg as well.
explanation.definitionFit: A counterproposal is an alternative offer put forward in reply to one already made.

clue.text: A setter's in torn clothing

indicators.note: these letters are placed inside the word for torn

blocks.note: rent is an old past participle of rend, to tear; it is split open
taken as written
the setter says I'm, I am

explanation.surface: The crossword setter confesses to wearing ripped clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Raiment is an old literary word for clothing or garments.

clue.text: Fish one decimated when penultimate is caught

indicators.note: the second-to-last letter is replaced, with the cricket abbreviation for caught taking its place

blocks.note: decimating takes one in ten, so one decimated is a tenth
c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A fish population is cut by a tenth when the second-last one gets hooked.
explanation.walkthrough: The penultimate T of TENTH gives way to C.
explanation.definitionFit: The tench is a European freshwater fish of the carp family.

clue.text: Incline to get aboard vessel free of filth

indicators.note: getting aboard a vessel puts you inside it, so one word goes within the other

blocks.note: a cup is a drinking vessel; it is split open
to incline is to lean

explanation.surface: Someone tilts to climb on board a ship that has been scrubbed clean.
explanation.definitionFit: To clean up something is to rid it of dirt, so the phrasal verb matches freeing it of filth.

clue.text: Customers with legal right in court reported magazine

indicators.note: the right is placed inside the abbreviation for court
reported means spoken of, so we go by how the magazine name is said

blocks.note: CT abbreviates court; it is split open
a lien is a legal right to hold property until a debt is paid
Elle is a fashion magazine

explanation.surface: Clients with a legal claim go to court, as a magazine reported.
explanation.walkthrough: The magazine Elle is said like the letter L, here spelt ELE.
explanation.definitionFit: A clientele is the body of customers or clients a business serves.

clue.text: Having shed sides in the way, nightmarish location for plant

indicators.text: Having shed sides in the way
indicators.note: the road word loses its two outside letters, the sides being shed

blocks.note: A Nightmare on Elm Street is the horror film

explanation.surface: A spooky garden plant, stripped of its edges, stands in the street.
explanation.walkthrough: The way is the street of the film title; it drops its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An elm tree is a large deciduous tree, and a tree is a plant.

clue.text: Flat's very loud during racing event on screen

indicators.note: racing letters dash about wildly, so they finish up in a new order
something happening during an event is inside it, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: ff is fortissimo, the musical mark for very loud
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A flat race is very loud on television.
explanation.walkthrough: 'racing event' looks like a horse race, but 'racing' is the signal and only 'event on screen' is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat drink has lost its fizz, so it is not effervescent.

clue.text: Sanctimonious pedantry ends with the involvement of authority

indicators.note: the ends of a word are its first and last letters
involvement means being drawn into something, so a word goes inside the two letters

blocks.note: its first and last letters
reach is range of power or authority, as in 'beyond the reach of the law'

explanation.surface: A self-righteous pedant finally invokes authority.
explanation.definitionFit: Preachy means given to moralising, so it describes someone sanctimonious and holier-than-thou.

clue.text: French island where ties can be renewed

blocks.note: first meaning: the French overseas island in the Indian Ocean
second meaning: a gathering at which old bonds and friendships are refreshed

explanation.walkthrough: 'ties' sounds like neckwear but means bonds between people; a gathering of old friends renews them.
explanation.definitionFit: Réunion is a French overseas department east of Madagascar, and a reunion is a get-together of old acquaintances.

clue.text: Extinct at last, my nemesis, woolly mammoth

indicators.note: the final letters die out, so each word loses its last letter
woolly means fuzzy and muddled, so the remaining letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written, then cut short
taken as written, then cut short

explanation.surface: A dying hunter gloats that their great foe, the woolly mammoth, is finally extinct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'woolly mammoth' reads as one beast, but 'woolly' is the anagram signal and 'mammoth' alone is the definition. Dropping the last letters of MY and NEMESIS leaves M and NEMESI to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Mammoth as an adjective means huge, a close synonym of immense.

clue.text: Cleavage, that is something pleasing

blocks.note: a cleavage is a split or cut
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, 'that is'

explanation.surface: A remark that a low neckline is a welcome sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cleavage' suggests a neckline, but here it means a split made by cleaving.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutie is an attractive or charming person or thing, so it is something pleasing to look at.

clue.text: Reverend backed when press finds nothing in church

indicators.note: backed means going backwards, so the following words are read in reverse
the earlier letters are placed inside the church abbreviation

blocks.note: CH is the usual abbreviation for church; it is split open
zero, nothing, looks like the letter O
if can mean when, as in 'if it rains'
to iron clothes is to press them

explanation.surface: A clergyman retreats when the newspapers find nothing scandalous in his church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'press' suggests the newspapers, but it is the verb for ironing; 'backed' turns 'when press' round as one string.
explanation.definitionFit: Reverend is a courtesy title given to clergy, so it is an example of an honorific.

clue.text: Open to view, clear bust wobbles

indicators.note: something that wobbles is unsteady, so these letters shake into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A sculpture or a cleavage is openly on display, wobbling for all to see.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrutable, the rare opposite of inscrutable, means able to be understood or examined, so open to view.

clue.text: Expert on vegetation for cattle

blocks.note: a buff is an enthusiast or expert
aloes are succulent plants

explanation.surface: A botanist's knowledge of plants that cattle graze on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' just places the expert before the plants in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Buffaloes are large wild or domesticated oxen, members of the cattle family.

clue.text: Money invested in weird mineral

indicators.note: money invested in something is put into it, so one letter goes inside a word

blocks.note: eery is a variant spelling of eerie, weird; it is split open
M is the economists' abbreviation for money supply

explanation.surface: Cash sunk into a strange rock as a speculative investment.
explanation.definitionFit: Emery is a dark granular rock used as an abrasive, as in emery boards, so it is a mineral.

clue.text: Retreating piece in chess, traditional board game

indicators.note: a piece in the words is a part of them, so the letters sit inside the phrase
retreating means going backwards, so the letters are read from right to left

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: A chess piece retreats in a traditional board game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piece' wants to be a chess piece, but 'piece in' means a part of the following words.
explanation.definitionFit: Darts is played by throwing at a dartboard, so it is literally a game played on a board.

clue.text: Nowt strange with one of TV duo being on that good form

blocks.note: Dec of Ant and Dec, the British TV presenting pair
nowt is northern English for nothing, zero
rum is British slang for strange

explanation.surface: A TV presenter grumbles in northern dialect that nothing odd is going on.
explanation.definitionFit: Decorum is proper, seemly behaviour, which is what 'good form' means in British usage.

clue.text: Perks up having let out bodily fluid

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading the letters from bottom to top
out can mean disordered or wrong, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: tips are perks, extra money on top of wages
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone cheers up after releasing some bodily fluid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perks up' reads as cheers up, but 'up' signals turning the perks round in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Spittle is saliva, a fluid produced by the body.

clue.text: What generous butcher might provide glutton

blocks.note: first meaning, taken literally: offal given away at no cost
second meaning: a person who indulges freely in food and drink

explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a whimsical literal reading of the compound: a butcher handing out offal gratis.
explanation.definitionFit: A free-liver is someone given to indulging their appetites, which describes a glutton.

clue.text: King admitting to being upset over daughter's skin-tight garment

indicators.note: admitting someone lets them in, so the next letters go inside the king
upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: King Lear, Shakespeare's monarch; split open
taken as written
D abbreviates daughter

explanation.surface: King Lear confesses he's upset about his daughter's tight outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: Fitting for Lear, a king famously troubled by his daughters.
explanation.definitionFit: A leotard is a close-fitting one-piece garment worn by dancers and gymnasts.

clue.text: County's groovy district?

blocks.note: a rut is a groove, so groovy is read as rut-like
land can mean a region or district

explanation.surface: Is a county a trendy, hip area?
explanation.walkthrough: 'groovy' looks like sixties slang for cool, but it is read literally as having grooves. Rutland is England's smallest county, in the East Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Rutland is a historic English county, the smallest in England.

clue.text: Charm about soldier having time for queen

indicators.note: having one thing for another means a swap, so one letter replaces another

blocks.note: ca. abbreviates circa, about
a private is a soldier of the lowest rank
T is the abbreviation for time
R for Regina, queen; this letter is swapped out

explanation.surface: A charming soldier makes time for the queen.
explanation.walkthrough: PRIVATE becomes PTIVATE when T replaces R.
explanation.definitionFit: To charm someone is to captivate them, holding their attention with delight.

clue.text: Legless group knocking back Special Brew

indicators.note: knocking back means sending backwards, so the letters are read in reverse

blocks.note: S abbreviates special
pale is a pale ale, a brewed beer

explanation.surface: Drunks downing a strong lager; Special Brew is a famously potent British lager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Legless' looks like British slang for drunk, but it is the definition: snakes have no legs.
explanation.definitionFit: Elaps is a genus of venomous snakes, a taxonomic group of animals without legs.

clue.text: Place of shooting and assault

blocks.note: first meaning, read as two words: where filming happens, on a film set
second meaning: an attack

explanation.walkthrough: 'shooting' suggests guns, but it is filming; read the answer as ON SET for the first meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Onset is an old word for an attack or assault, and 'on set' is where a film is being shot.

clue.text: Extravagant ring gentleman brought back for dish

indicators.note: brought back means returned the other way, so the whole string is read backwards

blocks.note: OTT abbreviates over the top, extravagant
a ring is round like the letter O
sir is the form of address for a gentleman

explanation.surface: A showy ring a gentleman returned, perhaps at dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Risotto is an Italian rice dish cooked slowly in stock.

clue.text: Disabled welcomed in by organisation offering sponsors for walk abroad

indicators.note: someone welcomed in by a group is taken inside it, so one word goes within another

blocks.note: Alcoholics Anonymous pairs each newcomer with a sponsor; it is split open
lamed means made lame, disabled

explanation.surface: A disabled person is welcomed by a charity that finds sponsors for a fundraising walk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sponsors for walk' suggests a charity walk, but AA is the group whose members have sponsors.
explanation.definitionFit: An alameda is a tree-lined public promenade in Spain or Latin America, a walk found abroad.

clue.text: European organisation invested in places to buy hammer

indicators.note: money invested in something is put inside it, so these letters go within another word

blocks.note: malls are shopping centres; this word is split open
EU is the European Union

explanation.surface: Brussels pours money into shopping centres, a hammer blow to the high street.
explanation.definitionFit: The malleus is the hammer-shaped bone of the middle ear, and its name is Latin for hammer.

clue.text: Under the influence of drugs, dead set to party

indicators.note: going to a party loosens things up, so these letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone high on drugs is utterly determined to go partying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dead set' reads as determined, but it is just the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedated means calmed by a drug, so the person is under its influence.
